segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You and Pip turn away from the door and look into the dimly lit workshop.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The room is enormous—carved directly out of an underground geothermal cavern. Warm steam hissed from copper pipes along the ceiling, and the walls were lined from floor to rafters with thousands of organized wooden bins containing gears, brass clock hands, springs, and glass vacuum tubes.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Standing in the center of the room, standing on a wooden apple crate to reach a giant iron workbench, was an elf.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was tiny—barely three feet tall—with wild white eyebrows that stuck straight out like wire brushes, a thick white beard tucked into his leather work apron, and a pair of brass jeweler's magnifying spectacles with five different lenses flipped over his squinting eyes.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In one leather-gloved hand, he held a heavy iron pipe wrench.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The old elf lowered his wrench and glared at you over his glasses with intense, cranky suspicion.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Who in the name of frosted gumdrops kicked my door down?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the elf barked in a voice like grinding gravel.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: And what kind of monster is out there eating my defensive perimeter?!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip stepped forward, tipping his houndstooth cap with supreme theatrical elegance.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Greetings, esteemed artisan! I am Master Detective Pip, and this is my chief field operative. We seek the legendary apprentice of the Great Clock—Barnaby Grumble!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The old elf squinted through his magnifying lenses.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Never heard of him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: the elf snapped, turning back to his workbench.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Barnaby Grumble died eighty years ago of boredom and irritation. Now get out before I grease your tail and feed you to my steam boiler.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You step forward. You don't try to argue with him. Instead, you reach into Pip's coat, pull out the heavy, leather-bound journal, and set it gently on the iron workbench.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The silver clasps catch the lantern light. The gold letters gleam: C.M.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby froze.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The wrench slipped from his hand, hitting the wooden floor with a heavy CLANG.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The old elf slowly turned around. His wild white eyebrows trembled. With shaking leather fingers, he touched the worn gold letters on the cover.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The master's journal,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby whispered, his cranky voice cracking with genuine grief.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Where did you find this?

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: In the secret vault beneath the old river mill,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you say quietly.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: The Great Clock has struck twelve. The hand is ticking backward. My friends in Arizona are losing their memories, and Everfrost is going dark.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You look directly into Barnaby's eyes.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You're the only one who knows how the Clockmaker built it. We need your help to stop him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby stared at you. The gruff, angry scowl faded from his face, replaced by a sudden, heartbreaking look of sheer terror.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Stop him?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby whispered, his eyes welling with panic.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You don't understand what you're asking! He isn't just an inventor anymore. He's woven himself into the very fabric of time itself! He will crush you! He will turn you into clockwork firewood!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby shook his head violently.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: No. No, I won't let another child be destroyed by that tower. I'm sorry, kid. This is for your own good.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Before you or Pip can react, Barnaby reaches into his leather apron and pulls out a small, ornate brass snuffbox.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He snaps the lid open. A cloud of glittering, lavender-and-silver dust—the exact same scent as the Cheer Hearth in Arizona—swirls into the air! Barnaby blows across the box, sending the glowing memory-dust washing straight over your face!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Sleep, child,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby murmured softly, looking away with deep regret.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Forget the clock. Forget the frost. Go back to your warm bed and let the holiday keep you safe...

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The shimmering lavender cloud wrapped around your head.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You feel the strange, sweet tickle in your thoughts—the heavy fog that made Maya smile blankly and forget yesterday.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You wait for the fog to take hold.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You blink.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You sneeze once:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Achoo!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You wipe your nose on your coat sleeve and look straight at Barnaby.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Is that supposed to make me sleepy?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you ask calmly.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Because it mostly just smells like burnt cinnamon.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby’s jaw dropped so low his white beard touched his apron.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The brass snuffbox slipped from his shaking fingers, clattering across the floorboards.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip gasped, clutching his chest.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: By St. Nick's whiskers... you... you breathed the Lethe-Mist!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby stumbled back against his workbench, staring at you in utter, speechless shock. His magnifying lenses rattled on his nose.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It... it didn't take,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby breathed, his voice trembling with reverent awe.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In eight hundred years, no living creature has ever looked into the mist and remembered their name.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The old elf took off his spectacles with trembling hands. For the first time, tears glinted in the corners of his eyes.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The ancient prophecy... from the founding days of Santa and the Master...

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby whispered, his voice hushed and solemn.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You notice what is hidden. You remember what is erased. You're the one who can touch the clock and live.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He looked at you as if seeing a miracle standing in his dusty shop.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You're an Unbound.
